description: Editable fictional policies for developing and simulating an airline customer service agent. All amounts, allowances, and deadlines are invented sample values, not any real airline's policies or a statement of passenger rights.

scope.partner_operated_flights: Not covered. Confirm the operating carrier's policies.

route_classification.domestic: Every segment in the ticketed direction stays within one country.
route_classification.international: At least one segment in the ticketed direction crosses a country border. Apply the international table to that whole direction, including its domestic connections.

scope.fee_amounts: Final fictional amounts in USD, including any applicable sample taxes. Each fee states its own charging unit.
scope.time_reference: Deadlines are relative to the scheduled departure of the relevant flight segment, using the departure airport's local time.
scope.exceptions: Confirmed itinerary-specific or airport-specific requirements take precedence. If a required exception is not documented, obtain confirmation rather than inventing a rule.
scope.policy_selection: Apply fare-dependent baggage, cancellation, and change rules using the purchased fare_tier, not seat_class alone. Premium economy standard follows standard rules; premium economy flexible follows flexible rules. The business cabin offers only the business tier.
scope.fee_and_fare_conversion: Policy fees are stated in USD dollars. Database price_cents values are USD cents: 8900 cents is USD 89.00. Convert to a common unit before combining a ticket price with optional fees. Included baggage allowances are already part of the purchased fare.

inventory_reference.live_data: Use current database records for flight schedules, flight status, available seats, and fare quotes. The seed file is a starting dataset, not live inventory; do not hard-code its prices or availability into policy answers.
inventory_reference.shared_inventory: All fare tiers in one flight cabin use the same available_seats count. A sold-out cabin has no bookable tier; a more expensive tier does not create additional seats.
inventory_reference.sample_week_scope: The sample week describes the available seed flights; it is not an expiry date or travel-date restriction for these policies.
inventory_reference.untracked_services: Flight seat inventory does not track pet-carrier availability, approved medical devices, mobility-aid acceptance, or confirmed special assistance. Those arrangements require separate confirmation.

policy.title: Cancellations, credits, and refunds
policy.summary: Refund eligibility depends on the purchase timing, fare type, travel already used, and whether the passenger or airline cancels. A refund to the original payment method is different from a travel credit.
questions_to_ask: Was the ticket purchased directly or through a third party?
When was it purchased, and when was the first flight scheduled to depart at purchase?
Which cabin and fare tier did you purchase, and is the journey domestic or international?
Has any part of the ticket been used?
Is this a voluntary cancellation or an airline cancellation or schedule change?
Which optional services were paid for, and what was the original payment method?

rules.title: Fictional 24-hour cancellation benefit
rules.answer: A wholly unused ticket booked directly with the airline may be canceled for a full refund to the original payment method within 24 hours of purchase, provided the first flight was scheduled at least 168 hours after purchase. This benefit applies to every fare and waives cancellation fees. The 168-hour condition is measured at purchase, not at the cancellation request. This is a fictional commercial benefit, not a statement of law.

rules.title: Voluntary cancellation outside the grace period
rules.answer: For a wholly unused ticket canceled before its first scheduled departure outside the grace period, basic is nonrefundable and receives no travel credit, except any refundable unused taxes. Standard receives a travel credit for the unused eligible ticket value less USD 50 domestically or USD 100 internationally. Flexible and business receive the unused ticket value back to the original payment method with no cancellation fee. A cancellation fee cannot exceed the eligible value and does not create an additional amount owed. These refund rules follow the purchased fare tier; a premium economy standard fare receives standard travel-credit treatment, while premium economy flexible follows the flexible refund rule.

details.standard_credit_value: Unused eligible ticket value minus the applicable cancellation fee, with a minimum of zero. Refundable unused taxes are returned separately and excluded from the credit calculation.
details.unused_taxes: Refundable unused taxes may be returned to the original payment method for every fare. Confirm the ticket's tax breakdown before quoting an amount.
details.partially_used_tickets: Require manual assessment of the unused value and refund eligibility; do not apply a whole-ticket refund automatically.
details.inventory_limitations: Flight fares store current tax-inclusive offers, not original ticket payments, itemized taxes, paid optional services, or purchase timestamps. Confirm those booking details before quoting a refund or applying the grace-period conditions.

rules.title: Travel credit validity
rules.answer: A travel credit belongs to the original named passenger, is nontransferable, and expires 12 months after issue. Replacement travel must be booked and completed by that expiry date. Credits have no cash value. Unused credit remains available until expiry; additional fare above the available credit must be paid separately.

details.expiry_extension: No automatic extension; exceptions require confirmation.

rules.title: Airline cancellation or qualifying schedule change
rules.answer: If the airline cancels a flight or makes a qualifying schedule change, the passenger may choose available rebooking without a change fee or fare difference, or a refund of unused affected travel to the original payment method, regardless of fare. For a wholly unused ticket, the passenger may decline the disrupted itinerary and request a full ticket refund. A travel credit is optional, not the only refund choice. Partially used itineraries require assessment of the unused affected value.

details.wholly_unused_ticket: Full ticket refund available when the passenger declines the disrupted itinerary.
details.unused_optional_services: Refund services associated with canceled or declined travel that cannot be used.
details.other_changes: Airport substitutions, cabin downgrades, connection changes, and other disruptions require assessment rather than an invented entitlement.

rules.title: Refunding optional services
rules.answer: Unused prepaid baggage, seat-selection, and pet fees are refundable to the original payment method if canceled before the first scheduled departure in the affected direction. This applies even if the base fare is nonrefundable. Refund the unused service fee if the airline cannot provide the purchased service. Used services are not refundable. Requests after departure require assessment, except refunds for services the airline could not provide.

rules.title: No-shows and missed flights
rules.answer: A passenger who has neither boarded nor canceled by the scheduled departure is a no-show. Basic and standard fares forfeit the missed segment's eligible value, except refundable unused taxes. Flexible and business no-show refunds require assessment. Missing an earlier segment may affect later segments, so confirm the remaining itinerary before promising onward travel. A refund of unused optional services after departure is subject to its separate policy.

rules.title: Refund processing and third-party bookings
rules.answer: Approved refunds are submitted to the original payment method within seven business days for card payments or 20 business days for other supported payment methods. These are submission targets after approval; the payment provider may take additional time to display the funds. Tickets purchased through an agency or another seller must be handled with the issuing seller for voluntary changes and refunds. Confirm the issuing channel before promising that the airline can process a payment refund directly.

details.cash_and_credit_split_payments: Confirm allocation to the original payment sources before quoting a refund breakdown.
